definitions.explanation: The wife of one's older brother. Japanese has specific kinship terms that distinguish between different in-law relationships based on the relative age and gender of the sibling.

examples.japanese: {兄嫁|あによめ}は{料理|りょうり}が{上手|じょうず}だ。
examples.english: My brother's wife is good at cooking.

examples.japanese: {兄嫁|あによめ}と{一緒|いっしょ}に{買|か}い{物|もの}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went shopping with my sister-in-law.

examples.japanese: {兄嫁|あによめ}が{子供|こども}を{連|つ}れてうちに{遊|あそ}びに{来|き}た。
examples.english: My brother's wife came to visit with the children.

notes:
{兄|あに} means 'older brother,' and {嫁|よめ} means 'bride' or 'wife.' Together, {兄嫁|あによめ} specifically refers to the wife of one's older brother. Japanese kinship vocabulary is more precise than English, distinguishing family relationships by birth order and side of the family.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {兄嫁|あによめ}と{仲|なか}が{良|よ}い (to get along well with one's sister-in-law)
- {兄嫁|あによめ}の{実家|じっか} (sister-in-law's parents' home)

RELATED KINSHIP TERMS:
- {義姉|ぎし} — sister-in-law (formal; older brother's wife or husband's/wife's older sister)
- {弟嫁|おとうとよめ} — younger brother's wife
- {嫁|よめ} — wife, bride, daughter-in-law
- {姉|あね} — older sister (blood relation)
